english.title: Engaged in the business of a postal operator delayed / opened a postal packet / mailbag
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person engaged in the business of a postal operator, in breach of your duty and without reasonable excuse, intentionally

(A)_[delayed a postal packet in the course of its transmission by post]_
(B)_[delayed **(..SPECIFY THE NUMBER..) postal packets in the course of their transmission by post]_
(C)_[opened a postal packet in the course of its transmission by post]_
(D)_[opened **(..SPECIFY THE NUMBER..) postal packets in the course of their transmission by post]_
(E)_[opened a mail bag]_
(F)_[opened **(..SPECIFY THE NUMBER..) mail bags]_
(G)_[**(..WHERE MORE THAN ONE OF THE ABOVE OPTIONS APPLY PLEASE SPECIFY THE DETAILS..)]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 83(1) and (6) of the Postal Services Act 2000.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
engaged in business of postal operator
delayed/opened a postal packet in the course of transmission by post OR
opened mail bag

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See Sections 83(2), (3) and (4) for exceptions
(ii) See offence wording H3809 for an offence committed by a person other than a postal operator, which carries a less severe penalty

(A)_[beri oedi i becyn a oedd wedi'i bostio wrth iddo gael ei drosglwyddo drwy'r post]_

(C)_[agor pecyn a oedd wedi'i bostio wrth iddo gael ei drosglwyddo drwy'r post]_

welsh.welshlegislation: Yn groes i adran 83(1) a (6) Deddf Gwasanaethau Post 2000.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
